meta.title: Flagged for Review — unverified values, gaps and irregularities
meta.policy: Every table row on this site must carry a source link to an official publisher. Where a value could not be confirmed from an official source during this session, the value cell is LEFT BLANK, the row is marked UNVERIFIED, and the reason is registered here with the official link needed to close it. Nothing is inferred, estimated from memory, or taken from a news article, brokerage, data aggregator or wiki. Flagged items do NOT block publication; they are disclosed here so a reader can complete the verification manually.
meta.status: All items on this page are recorded in COORDINATION.md with status 'needs review'. They are non-blocking by design.

flags.title: No transaction documents were supplied and all personal financial information is withheld
flags.detail: The subject property's address, parcel number, owner identity, purchase price, basis, assessed value, contract rent, net operating income, market value and insurance details were never provided. Under the privacy protocol they are also not published even if later obtained. Every parcel-specific and owner-specific cell on this site is therefore blank.
flags.official_route_to_close: Owner-held documents plus the Los Angeles County Assessor public parcel record.

flags.title: The lease itself was not supplied
flags.detail: Rent escalator, expense stops, renewal option count and length, termination rights, exclusive-use covenants, continuous-operation covenants, assignment and subletting rights, and the tenant's insurance and maintenance obligations are all unknown. The projection model therefore tests escalation SCENARIOS rather than asserting a lease structure, and the redevelopment option is expressly not modelled.
flags.official_route_to_close: The executed lease and all amendments. No public source can supply these.

flags.title: Lease expiry is a window (2030-2035), not a date
flags.detail: A five-year range in expiry changes the remaining firm term by more than 100%, and firm term is the dominant driver of net-lease value. The model runs 4, 6 and 9 years to span the window rather than picking a midpoint.
flags.official_route_to_close: The lease expiry date, or the recorded memorandum of lease in the Los Angeles County Recorder's index.

flags.title: Tax Rate Area and total parcel tax rate unknown
flags.detail: Los Angeles County divides property into hundreds of Tax Rate Areas, and the Board of Supervisors sets rates under Article XIII A of the State Constitution. Without the Tax Rate Area code the total rate — base 1% levy plus voted indebtedness plus direct and special assessments, including any local school bond — cannot be stated. Under an NNN lease this is the tenant's reimbursable obligation, so it is a live variable in tenant affordability.
flags.official_route_to_close: Los Angeles County Auditor-Controller Tax Rate Area Lookup, using the Assessor Parcel Number.

flags.title: Lease counterparty identity and credit support unknown
flags.detail: Jack in the Box Inc.'s own Form 10-K properties table shows three coexisting structures: company-owned buildings on company-owned land; company-leased buildings on leased land; and franchise directly-owned or directly-leased buildings. A Form 10-Q confirms that on refranchising the company retains the head lease and sub-leases to the franchisee. Whether the landlord's counterparty here is an SEC-reporting company or a small private franchisee is unknown, and so is the existence of any corporate guaranty, letter of credit or security deposit. The two cases carry materially different credit risk.
flags.official_route_to_close: The lease signature block and any guaranty. The structure typology is already verified from SEC filings.

flags.title: Zoning, General Plan land use and alternative-use entitlement unknown
flags.detail: Without the zoning designation the alternative-use and redevelopment options cannot be underwritten at all, and the value of the site if the restaurant closes cannot be assessed.
flags.official_route_to_close: City of Los Angeles Department of City Planning Zoning Information and Map Access System.

flags.title: Parcel-level hazard designations not determined
flags.detail: Three separate official determinations are outstanding: FEMA flood zone, CAL FIRE / LA County Fire Department Fire Hazard Severity Zone, and California Geological Survey Alquist-Priolo Earthquake Fault Zone. The third also creates a statutory seller disclosure duty under Public Resources Code Section 2621.9, so it affects the SELL path directly, not just the hold path.
flags.official_route_to_close: FEMA Flood Map Service Center; LA County Fire Department FHSZ open-data layer; California Geological Survey Information Warehouse.

flags.title: Trade-area micro-geography cannot be delimited
flags.detail: Average daily traffic, signalisation, ingress and egress, median breaks, curb cuts, distance to rail, competing quick-service sites, active entitlement applications, assigned schools and nearby higher-education institutions all require a location, which is withheld. No sub-county official series can be matched to the site.
flags.official_route_to_close: City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation traffic counts; City Planning active case information; CDE DataQuest school locator.

flags.title: California statewide and Los Angeles County minimum wages not read from the official publisher
flags.detail: The City of Los Angeles rate IS verified at $18.42 from July 1, 2026, read directly from the Office of Wage Standards notice. The statewide and county rates were seen only in secondary summaries, so they are recorded as 'reported' and left blank.
flags.official_route_to_close: California Department of Industrial Relations minimum wage FAQ; Los Angeles County wage ordinance pages.

flags.title: Census QuickFacts housing block not captured for the City of Los Angeles
flags.detail: Median gross rent, median value of owner-occupied units, median selected monthly owner costs and housing-unit counts were not read from census.gov in this session. The QuickFacts pages were retrieved in chunks and the housing block fell outside the chunks captured.
flags.official_route_to_close: U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts for Los Angeles city, housing section; or data.census.gov table DP04 / B25077.

flags.title: Census publishes no city-level business or employment fields for Los Angeles
flags.detail: Census QuickFacts shows the 'not available' marker for every Businesses field at City of Los Angeles level: employer establishments, employment, annual payroll and nonemployer establishments. This is a genuine gap in the official series, not a retrieval failure. County values are published and are used instead, with the geography stated.
flags.official_route_to_close: Census County Business Patterns ZIP-code or place-level tables, which do carry city geography, downloaded directly from the CBP datasets page.

flags.title: Limited-service restaurant establishment count (NAICS 722513) not obtained
flags.detail: The Census Business Patterns API rejected the query because a valid API key is required, and the value was not read from the published CSV. Competitor density is a material input to trade-area analysis, so this is a substantive gap rather than a cosmetic one. It was not filled from any aggregator.
flags.official_route_to_close: Census County Business Patterns 2023 dataset, NAICS 722513, Los Angeles County, downloaded from the official datasets page.

flags.title: LAUSD enrolment series by year and the 2026-27 projection not read from CDE or LAUSD
flags.detail: Only the 2025-26 Census Day endpoint of 497,105 was read directly from cde.ca.gov. Earlier years and the forward projection were seen only in third-party compilations and are recorded as 'reported', not verified.
flags.official_route_to_close: CDE DataQuest district enrolment series; LAUSD board-adopted budget projections.

flags.title: NCES Common Core of Data figures for LAUSD not read from nces.ed.gov
flags.detail: Reported membership of 408,026, 784 schools and a student-to-classroom-teacher ratio of 19.20 for 2024-25 were seen only in a secondary source. The federal CCD universe also differs from CDE Census Day enrolment, so the two are not interchangeable.
flags.official_route_to_close: NCES Common Core of Data district-level file for LAUSD, CDS 19647330000000.

flags.title: Revenue opening year for Metro D Line Sections 2 and 3 not stated on the official project page
flags.detail: Section 1's opening on May 8, 2026 IS verified from metro.net. A 2027 date for the remaining sections appeared only on non-official pages; the official project page retrieved in this session states only that work continues across all three sections.
flags.official_route_to_close: Los Angeles Metro D Line Subway Extension project page and Metro board agendas.

flags.title: No official government source publishes net-lease capitalisation rates
flags.detail: Going-in cap rates, rent per square foot for comparable quick-service-restaurant assets, and credit spreads over Treasury for single-tenant net-lease paper are private market data sold by brokerages and research firms. No federal, state or local agency publishes them. Rather than quote a third-party number as fact, the projection model runs an explicit, labelled cap-spread sensitivity grid over the OFFICIAL U.S. Treasury par yield and marks every dependent output as UNVERIFIED INPUT.
flags.official_route_to_close: None exists. The only official anchor available is the Treasury par yield curve, which is used.

flags.title: CAL FIRE State Responsibility Area and Local Responsibility Area map effective dates not read from fire.ca.gov
flags.detail: The 2025 establishment of the Los Angeles County Local Responsibility Area Fire Hazard Severity Zones IS verified from the official LA County open-data layer. The associated SRA map effective date of April 1, 2024 and the phased LRA rollout schedule were read from a non-government summary.
flags.official_route_to_close: CAL FIRE Fire and Resource Assessment Program hazard-mapping pages.

flags.title: FEMA National Risk Index values for Los Angeles County not read from fema.gov
flags.detail: The NRI is an interactive application. County composite score, total expected annual loss, per-hazard expected annual loss, social vulnerability and community resilience values were read from independent republications of the official v1.20 dataset (December 2025), not from a fema.gov page. They are recorded in the 'reported' column only and are NOT used as inputs to the projection model. The official figures matter because they are the only national, all-hazard, publicly comparable measure of county catastrophe exposure.
flags.official_route_to_close: FEMA National Risk Index — select Los Angeles County, California in the interactive map or download the v1.20 county-level dataset.

flags.title: Count of federal disaster declarations for Los Angeles County not read from fema.gov
flags.detail: A count of 88 declarations since 1969 was seen only in secondary sources. The official FEMA disaster declaration list is the authority.
flags.official_route_to_close: FEMA Disaster Declarations — filter by Los Angeles County, California.

flags.title: Structural system, year built, code vintage and seismic retrofit status unknown
flags.detail: These determine both earthquake performance and the cost of any conversion or re-tenanting. Los Angeles has adopted mandatory seismic retrofit programmes for specific building types, so the applicability of any such ordinance to this parcel is a real question, not a formality.
flags.official_route_to_close: City of Los Angeles Department of Building and Safety permit and certificate-of-occupancy records for the parcel.

flags.title: Business-interruption exposure of the tenant during a regional catastrophe not quantifiable
flags.detail: Los Angeles County's official figure of approximately 6,800 businesses impacted by the January 2025 fires is a county-wide count, not a restaurant-sector count. No official source disaggregates it to quick-service restaurants, so no site-level interruption estimate is published.
flags.official_route_to_close: None exists at parcel level. County-level official statistics are used as the only available calibration.

flags.title: Extreme-heat frequency and trend not obtained
flags.detail: Heat affects drive-thru demand positively and tenant cooling cost negatively, so this is a material gap. No NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information series was read in this session.
flags.official_route_to_close: NOAA NCEI climate normals and daily summaries for the nearest official station.

flags.title: County and City documentary transfer tax rates not read from the official publishers
flags.detail: Both rates were consistently reported by secondary sources — $1.10 per $1,000 county and $4.50 per $1,000 city — but neither was read directly from lacounty.gov or finance.lacity.gov in this session. They are therefore excluded from the projection model's transaction-cost calculation, which means the modelled net proceeds for the SELL path are OPTIMISTIC by roughly half a percent of price.
flags.official_route_to_close: Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder and Treasurer and Tax Collector; City of Los Angeles Office of Finance real property transfer tax page.

flags.title: Current Measure ULA indexed thresholds and the lien-inclusive measurement base not read from the City Office of Finance
flags.detail: The statutory MECHANISM is verified from the official LAHD FAQ and LAMC Section 21.9.2: 4% above the lower threshold and 5.5% at or above the upper threshold, charged on the entire consideration or value. The DOLLAR THRESHOLDS are indexed annually to the Bureau of Labor Statistics Chained Consumer Price Index and published each year before July 1 by the Office of Finance; the pair reported for periods from July 1, 2026 could not be read from the official page in this session. Because the tax is a cliff, the exact threshold is decision-critical.
flags.official_route_to_close: City of Los Angeles Office of Finance — Real Property Transfer Tax and Measure ULA FAQ, current-year threshold schedule.

flags.title: Los Angeles City business tax obligations of the tenant operator not verified
flags.detail: No official rate table was read line by line in this session. Under an NNN lease this is the tenant's obligation, but tenant insolvency converts it into a landlord re-tenanting problem.
flags.official_route_to_close: City of Los Angeles Office of Finance — Business Tax.

flags.title: Section 1031 like-kind exchange availability and deadlines not verified line by line
flags.detail: Recorded as an option to evaluate, never as an assumption. No election exists and no qualified intermediary is engaged. The owner's basis and entity structure are withheld.
flags.official_route_to_close: Internal Revenue Service like-kind exchange guidance and Treasury regulations.

flags.title: California wildfire disclosure and non-renewal moratorium provisions not read from insurance.ca.gov
flags.detail: New disclosure requirements reported to have taken effect January 1, 2025, and a reported extension of the 12-month non-renewal moratorium from January 1, 2026 to commercial properties, homeowners associations, condominiums and non-profits, were read only from secondary summaries. Materially relevant because the tenant must carry property insurance under an NNN lease.
flags.official_route_to_close: California Department of Insurance press releases and bulletins on the Sustainable Insurance Strategy.

flags.title: Los Angeles Police Department COMPSTAT crime figures not transcribed with confidence
flags.detail: The official COMPSTAT weekly snapshots are published as multi-column tables. The extraction of specific citywide year-to-date Part I crime totals in this session was not unambiguous, so no figure is published. Directionally the official documents indicate a year-over-year decline, but a direction is not a verified number and is not presented as one.
flags.official_route_to_close: LAPD COMPSTAT weekly snapshot PDFs; Los Angeles City open-data portal Part I crime tables.

flags.title: Fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter results not yet filed; scheduled release date is third-party only
flags.detail: As of the November 6, 2026 retrieval date the most recent periodic filing is the Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 5, 2026, filed August 12, 2026. A November 25, 2026 release date appeared only on a third-party earnings calendar.
flags.official_route_to_close: SEC EDGAR filing index for Jack in the Box Inc., CIK 0000807882.

flags.title: No credit rating is stated for the tenant anywhere on this site
flags.detail: Ratings are issued by private Nationally Recognized Statistical Rating Organizations and are not an official government source. Per the verification policy no rating is quoted. Tenant credit is instead assessed from the company's own SEC-filed disclosures: restaurant count trajectory, same-store sales, franchise-level margin, franchisee bad-debt expense, average unit volume and leadership status.
flags.official_route_to_close: None from a government publisher. SEC filings are used as the substitute and are cited throughout the tenant page.

flags.title: No public disclosure identifies individual restaurants selected for closure
flags.detail: This is the highest-consequence unknown in the entire analysis. Jack in the Box Inc. discloses closure COUNTS and programme SIZE but never a site list. Whether the subject restaurant is on the JACK on Track list cannot be verified from any source, official or otherwise, and is not inferred. The recommended decision path is built specifically to obtain this information privately and early, through the franchise agreement expiration date and a direct statement of renewal intent, rather than to guess it.
flags.official_route_to_close: No public route exists. The practical route is the tenant relationship: the franchise agreement expiration date and a written statement of renewal intent.

flags.title: Franchise agreement expiration date unknown
flags.detail: The company has stated that the remaining underperforming locations close THEREAFTER based on their respective franchise agreement termination dates. That date may not coincide with the lease expiry, and it is the variable that actually governs closure timing.
flags.official_route_to_close: Not publicly available. Must be obtained from the tenant or, if the counterparty is the franchisor under a head lease, from the sub-lease documentation.

flags.title: No official source quantifies re-tenanting downtime, conversion cost or land residual value
flags.detail: The dark-box land residual grid (30%, 50%, 70% of total value) is an unverified scenario input. The only official land-versus-improvement ratio available is Jack in the Box Inc.'s own balance sheet — land of $93,255 thousand against buildings of $967,676 thousand, or 8.79% of gross book cost — which is a national historical cost figure and is expressly NOT used as a market estimate. Re-tenanting probability, downtime length and second-generation conversion cost have no official publisher at all.
flags.official_route_to_close: None from a government publisher. A licensed appraiser's land-versus-improvement allocation for the specific parcel is the only defensible route.

irregularities.title: BEA has discontinued metropolitan-area GDP and personal income statistics
irregularities.detail: The Bureau of Economic Analysis states in its 2024 county release that GDP and personal income statistics for metropolitan statistical areas, micropolitan areas, metropolitan divisions and combined statistical areas have been discontinued. Any projection that previously relied on Los Angeles-Long Beach-Anaheim MSA GDP can no longer be sourced. This analysis was rebuilt on COUNTY-level GDP ($818.5 billion for Los Angeles County, 2024), which changes the geography of every income anchor used.
irregularities.impact: Method change forced mid-analysis. Documented rather than hidden.

irregularities.title: SCAG's newer forecast reverses the direction of its own adopted forecast for Los Angeles County population
irregularities.detail: The adopted Connect SoCal 2024 plan, published December 2023, projected Los Angeles County population rising about 720,000 (+7%) to 10.77 million by 2050. The Connect SoCal 2050 Technical Working Group draft of November 20, 2025 projects county population DECLINING about 5% to 9.3 million by 2050 — while projecting county HOUSEHOLDS rising about 6%. Two official documents from the same regional agency disagree on the sign of the county's population trend. The projection model uses neither as a driver; population enters only through the qualitative risk register.
irregularities.impact: Long-range population forecasts for this region are not stable. Any 2050-horizon conclusion drawn from a single SCAG document is unsafe.

irregularities.title: FEMA National Risk Index county values circulate widely but are not readable as static figures from fema.gov
irregularities.detail: The NRI is delivered as an interactive application. The county-level values that appear across third-party risk sites could not be confirmed against a fema.gov page in this session. They are therefore held out of the verified columns and out of the model entirely. See F-18.
irregularities.impact: The most commonly cited all-hazard ranking for Los Angeles County is not usable as a verified input, so catastrophe severity is anchored instead on the county's own official January 2025 fire loss statistics and on USGS earthquake probabilities.

irregularities.title: No official employment projection series extends through the lease expiry window
irregularities.detail: The State of California's official ten-year occupational projection window runs 2022 to 2032. The lease expires somewhere in 2030 to 2035. There is no official source that projects Los Angeles County employment through 2035, so the final years of the decision window cannot be covered by verified job-growth data.
irregularities.s: California Employment Development Department, Labor Market Information Division
irregularities.impact: Employment-based conclusions are stated only to 2032 and are explicitly not extrapolated to 2035.

irregularities.title: Federal and state school enrolment statistics disagree for the same district
irregularities.detail: The California Department of Education reports Los Angeles Unified Census Day enrolment of 497,105 for 2025-26. The federal Common Core of Data is reported to show membership of 408,026 for 2024-25 across 784 schools. These are different universes — Census Day enrolment includes categories that CCD membership excludes — and are not interchangeable. Neither is wrong; quoting one against the other is.
irregularities.s: California Department of Education; National Center for Education Statistics
irregularities.impact: Only the CDE figure is published as verified. The CCD figure is held in the 'reported' column.

irregularities.title: Official LAPD COMPSTAT publications are not reliably machine-readable
irregularities.detail: The weekly COMPSTAT snapshots are published as multi-column tables in which the alignment of period labels to numeric columns cannot be confirmed unambiguously from the document text. A year-over-year decline in citywide Part I crime is indicated, but no specific total is published. See F-28.
irregularities.s: Los Angeles Police Department; City of Los Angeles open data portal
irregularities.impact: Crime is excluded from the verified dataset entirely rather than published with a transcription risk.

irregularities.title: Measure ULA thresholds are indexed annually but the current schedule is not published in a single stable official location
irregularities.detail: LAMC Section 21.9.2 indexes the thresholds to the Bureau of Labor Statistics Chained Consumer Price Index and requires publication each year before July 1. The mechanism is verified from the official LAHD FAQ; the current dollar thresholds are not readable from the City Office of Finance page retrieved in this session. Because the tax is a cliff applied to the whole price, an unverified threshold is a material gap. See F-24.
irregularities.s: City of Los Angeles Housing Department; City of Los Angeles Office of Finance
irregularities.impact: The single largest transaction-cost item in the SELL path cannot be pinned to a dollar threshold from an official page in this session.

irregularities.title: The tenant's next earnings date is known only from third-party calendars
irregularities.detail: A November 25, 2026 date for Jack in the Box Inc.'s fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter results appeared only on third-party earnings calendars. No SEC filing or company investor-relations page read in this session confirms it. See F-29.
irregularities.s: SEC EDGAR, Jack in the Box Inc. CIK 0000807882
irregularities.impact: The monitoring calendar on this site points to EDGAR directly rather than to a date.

irregularities.title: Census QuickFacts silently withholds city-level business data while publishing it for the county
irregularities.detail: For the City of Los Angeles, every Businesses field in QuickFacts carries the 'not available' marker, while the same fields are fully populated for Los Angeles County. A reader comparing city and county pages would not know that the city series simply does not exist. See F-11.
irregularities.s: U.S. Census Bureau, QuickFacts and County Business Patterns
irregularities.impact: City-level establishment and employment density — a natural proxy for competitor supply — is unavailable from the most accessible official product and must be pulled from County Business Patterns tables directly.

excluded_sources.policy: The following classes of source were encountered during research and were DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED. Where a value from one of them appears anywhere on this site it is confined to the 'reported' column of a row that is marked UNVERIFIED, and is never used as a model input or as a basis for the recommendation.
classes: Commercial hazard and risk aggregators that republish FEMA National Risk Index data
Real-estate brokerages, investment platforms and cap-rate research providers
Local and national news outlets, including television stations and newspapers
Earnings calendars, stock-screeners and financial data aggregators
Real-estate listing portals and neighbourhood-score providers
excluded_sources.note: A complete list of every official publisher used, with the exact URL and what was read from it, is on the Sources & Verification page and in docs/SOURCES.md.
